captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 3. In this lesson: Rhyme time.
Find rhyming words and read a rhyming poem aloud.
Here are some new words. Rhyme. Words that end with the same sound, like cat and hat.
Poem. A short piece of writing with lines, often with rhymes. Line.
One row of words in a poem. Listen and say them. rhyme
poem
line.
And some more words. Verse. A group of lines in a poem. Loud. Making a big sound. Quiet.
Making very little sound. Listen and say them. verse
loud
quiet.
Time for a question. The video will stop.
Which word means: words that end with the same sound, like cat and hat?
Now some grammar: Plural nouns. Most nouns add -s. Nouns ending in s, sh, ch, x add -es.
Nouns ending in consonant + y change to -ies. For example: cat becomes cats.
For example: box becomes boxes. For example: city becomes cities.
Now listen, and read along. Rain on the window.
Tap, tap, tap, goes the rain on the pane, Drip, drip, drip, down the long window lane.
Splash, splash, splash, go the boots on the street, Squelch, squelch, squelch,
go my wet, muddy feet. Then out comes the sun, and the clouds run away, Hooray, hooray,
hooray for a bright, sunny day!
Another question. The video will stop. What is the poem about?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like rhyme, poem, line.
You practised plural nouns. And you read Rain on the window.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!

captions: Hello, and welcome to Camday English, Stage 3. In this lesson: Sound words.
Use words that sound like noises (onomatopoeia) and adverbs of manner.
Here are some new words. Buzz. The sound a bee makes. Crash.
A loud noise when something falls and breaks. Whisper. Speak very quietly.
Listen and say them. buzz
crash
whisper.
And some more words. Sizzle. The sound food makes when it cooks in hot oil. Creak.
The sound an old door makes. Pop. A short, sharp sound, like a balloon bursting.
Listen and say them. sizzle
creak
pop.
Time for a question. The video will stop. Which word means: the sound a bee makes?
Now some grammar: Adverbs (how?). Adverbs tell us how something happens.
Many adverbs end in -ly. For example: She sang loudly. For example: He walked slowly.
Now listen, and read along. The noisy kitchen.
In my kitchen in the morning, what a noise you hear!
The kettle starts to whistle, loudly, loud and clear.
The pan begins to sizzle as the eggs go in to fry,
The toaster gives a little pop and toast jumps up so high.
The cat walks in so quietly, she doesn't make a sound,
Then CRASH! A cup falls off the shelf and lands upon the ground!
Another question. The video will stop. When is the kitchen noisy?
Well done! Today you learned new words, like buzz, crash, whisper.
You practised adverbs (how?). And you read The noisy kitchen.
Now try the practice questions. See you next time!
